issues.failure_explanation: The L^q norm requires absolute values: 1/q \|R\|_q^q = 1/q \sum |R_j|^q. The displayed expansion omits the absolute values, so for non-integer q>1 the terms are undefined when a residual is negative. Moreover, the gradient of 1/q |R|^q is |R|^{q-2} R \nabla R, not R^{q-1} \nabla R as used in the proof of Theorem thm:exist-uniqueness-scheme-gen and Theorem thm:added-1. This invalidates the gradient calculation, although the conclusion can be repaired by using the correct absolute-value form.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define L(u)=1/q \sum |R_j|^q and use w_j = |R_j|^{q-2} R_j in the critical-point proofs. The existing arguments then go through.
issues.overall_effect: The main well-posedness theorems for general q>1 are stated for an ill-defined functional, and their critical-point proofs use an incorrect gradient formula.
issues.title: L^q residual functional uses powers without absolute values and incorrect gradient exponent
issues.why_classification: The repair is local (insert absolute values and correct the exponent) and preserves all substantive conclusions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By the same argument as in step 1, the matrix $\sum_{k=1}^K \alpha_k A_k$ is also $\mu$-diagonally dominant

issues.failure_explanation: Diagonal dominance is a row-wise property and is not preserved by transposition. The matrix DR is row-wise mu-diagonally dominant, but (DR)^T need not be. For example, with two interior nodes and different H_p derivatives, the transpose can fail the row dominance inequality. The proof's conclusion that the convex combination is invertible still holds because it is the transpose of a mu-diagonally dominant (hence invertible) matrix, but the stated reasoning is false.

failure_location.quote: We know from Lemma \ref{lem:DR-invertible}, that the matrix $\left(D \cR(u_n^{(k)})\right)^\top$ is $\mu$-diagonally dominant with $\mu$ independent of $n$ and $k$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the claim that (DR)^T is mu-diagonally dominant with the fact that (DR)^T is invertible since DR is, and use invertibility of the convex combination of DR matrices.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the non-differentiable case of Theorem thm:exist-uniqueness-scheme-gen is invalid as written, though the theorem statement remains true.
issues.title: Proof claims transpose of DR is mu-diagonally dominant
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short local argument and does not affect the theorem's conclusion.

Similarly, we may apply this transform to the time dependent equation
    u_t+H(x,\nabla u) = 0

issues.failure_explanation:
For v = (1 - e^{-\lambda u})/\lambda, we have v_t = (1-\lambda v) u_t and 
abla v = (1-\lambda v) 
abla u. If u_t + \|
abla u\| = 0, then v_t + \|
abla v\| = 0. The additional term \lambda v is spurious.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the term \lambda v so the transformed equation is v_t + \|\nabla v\| = 0.
issues.overall_effect: The remark on the Kruzhkov transform for time-dependent equations is incorrect, but it is not used in the main theorems.
issues.title: Incorrect Kruzhkov-transformed time-dependent eikonal equation
issues.why_classification: A one-term correction in a side remark; no main result depends on it.

issues.failure_explanation: Subtracting the two equations gives (w_j^{n+1} - w_j^n)/\dt + F(u^{n+1},\nabla u^{n+1}) - F(v^{n+1},\nabla v^{n+1}) = R(u)^{n+1}_j. At a positive maximum of w, monotonicity in p and F3 give (1/\dt - \lambda/\dt) w_j \le w_j^n/\dt + R_j, hence w_j \le (w_j^n + \dt R_j)/(1-\lambda). The stated bound omits the factor 1/(1-\lambda). For example, with a single node and F(u)=-cu, c\dt=\lambda, the scheme gives w^{n+1}=w^n/(1-\lambda), violating the stated inequality for \lambda>0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the factor 1/(1-\lambda) on the right-hand side of the estimate and update the recursion accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The stability guarantee for implicit time-dependent schemes is too strong; the correct estimate has an amplification factor 1/(1-\lambda), and the subsequent recursive bound should also include this factor.
issues.title: Time-dependent stability estimate omits factor 1/(1-lambda)
issues.why_classification: The theorem as stated is false. The repair requires a contained correction to the estimate and its recursive consequence, weakening the stability guarantee but not destroying the well-posedness results.
